verdict.rationale: LangGraph's own interrupts can pause graph execution at chosen points and wait for external input, then resume via Command. This supports an approval gate placed before a step, and compile-time breakpoints plus checkpointer-backed human-in-the-loop reinforce it. The evidence never shows approval tied specifically to individual sensitive tool calls, nor any approve/reject/edit semantics, so the gate is a general pause point rather than a documented per-tool approval policy. Missing for 10: documented per-tool approval configuration, explicit approve/reject/edit decision handling for tool calls, independent hands-on corroboration of tool-call gating.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can require human approval before specific sensitive tool calls execute

citations.quote: Interrupts allow you to pause graph execution at specific points and wait for external input before continuing.
you resume execution by re-invoking the graph using Command, which then becomes the return value of the interrupt() call from inside the node
It is also where you can specify runtime args like checkpointers and breakpoints.
Human-in-the-loop — Seamlessly incorporate human oversight by inspecting and modifying agent state at any point during execution.
